To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in patients with giant cell arteritis, a short course of tumour necrosis (TNF)-α blockers is effective in inducing remission; 2) in patients with relapsing disease, a short course (3 months) of TNF-α blockers is effective as a steroid-sparing agent; 3) in patients with refractory giant cell arteritis to GCs, a long course of TNF- α blockers is effective in maintaining disease remission; and

in patients with giant cell arteritis who have received glucocorticoids for at least 1 month, treatment with tumour-necrosis factor (TNF) blockers is effective in reducing the dose of glucocorticoids and in preventing relapses, and that treatment with TNF blockers is associated with an acceptable safety profile.
the addition of a TNF-α inhibitor to GCs is associated with a reduction of the cumulative prednisone dose, a lower rate of relapse and a higher rate of remission, compared with GC monotherapy.
